parameterNotes.service: the service whose client pool held every connection; the in-use counter is that pool's, so the name is the subject of the reading.
parameterNotes.datastore: the database the pool pointed at, named to rule it out: the reading that matters is on the client side, and the server reports nothing.
parameterNotes.trigger: what preceded the deadlock, named in a word; the connection counter states the exhaustion, and the promotion is why it happened then.

groundTruth.rootCauseReason: The service's client pool has twenty connections, and after the replica promotion all twenty were held by threads waiting on a lock that a transaction held while waiting for a connection of its own. That is a cycle entirely inside the pool: no thread can release a connection, so no thread can finish, so the pool never frees one. The database is not part of it -- the primary reports no long-running query, because the transactions the threads are waiting on are queued in the client rather than running on the server.

rootCauseIndicators.description: every connection in the pool is held, which is the state from which nothing can proceed
the service's own error, raised when a request asks for a connection and there is none to give

causalChain.mechanism: twenty threads hold twenty connections while waiting on a lock held by a transaction that is itself waiting for a connection, so the pool can never free one and the service deadlocks against itself

evidenceCheckpoints.description: all twenty connections are held, which is the whole pool — the reading that says the service ran out of a resource it holds itself
the pool's size, cited from the case's own parameters: the ceiling the connections-in-use reading reaches, so the two numbers are one fact stated twice rather than two facts
the primary reports no long-running query, which is the control that puts the deadlock in the client rather than in the database
the service's own words for the state, logged when a request asks the pool for a connection and finds none

remediation.action: acquire the connection after the lock rather than before it, so a thread waiting on a lock cannot hold the connection the lock holder needs
bound the wait on a pooled connection with a timeout, so a cycle fails a request instead of stopping every thread

sli.none: what moved is the number of pool connections in use, and the only other series is a count of long-running queries on the database: a deadlock is read here as a count, not as a time.

query: The billing service began throwing 'connection pool exhausted' after the replica promotion. What is the root cause, and why is the database not it?
